newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-LIPINSKI YOUNGEST WOMEN'S WORLD CHAMPION.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-LIPINSKI YOUNGEST WOMEN'S WORLD CHAMPION.

text.p: Tara Lipinski became the youngest-ever women's world figure skating champion with a performance of astonishing maturity and sustained brilliance on Saturday.
The American, at 14 years, nine months and 12 days, is 32 days younger than Sonia Henie when the Norwegian won the first of her 10 successive world titles in 1927.

Ironically, Lipinski was technically ineligible for this competition under a rule passed last year that skaters had to be 15 the previous July 1 to take part. But she was given a dispensation because she had competed last year, before the rule was brought in.
Lipinski accomplished seven triple jumps, including a remarkable and difficult triple loop-triple loop combination which no other skater in the world can yet do.
She did not put a foot wrong in her four-minute display although she again relied on her fast spins because she gets no height on the takeoff of her jumps.
Despite the outstanding display of Lipinski, team mate and defending champion Michelle Kwan beat her in the free skating with an excellent return to her top form.
But Kwan was too far back in fourth place after the short programme and despite her superior artistry had to settle for the silver medal after a superb routine to Indian music.
Vanessa Gusmeroli of France, 18, took the bronze.
